exitCodes.2: usage error, or --project is not a directory
exitCodes.3: no capability map (not an error); stdout is {"schemaVersion":1,"error":"no-capability-map"}
exitCodes.4: capability map or a module file unreadable; stdout is {"schemaVersion":1,"error":"unreadable","detail":...}

review.none: no review marker in the file (the project may not use markers); says nothing about approval
review.pending: written and waiting for the user's review
review.approved: approved by the user; the file has not changed since
review.codex-approved: Codex reviewed it with no blocking finding and spec-guard recorded it from a delegate report (interface 1.15, spec/codex-approval.md); it counts as approved only where the module's takeover gives this step to codex. The file has not changed since
review.revised: approved earlier (by the user, or by Codex for a Spec or Plan), edited after approval, needs another review
review.invalid: the marker line is malformed; review state unknown

externalReview.none: no external review recorded and not declined
externalReview.recorded: an external review (for example from delegate) is recorded; advisory only, not an approval
externalReview.declined: the user declined an external review for this module

reviewApprovedBy.user: per module, per file (spec, plan): the user's approval marker (interface 1.15, spec/codex-approval.md)
reviewApprovedBy.codex: per module, per file: Codex's approval marker, and the module's takeover gives this step to codex (for a Plan, its pre-declared section lists nothing)
reviewApprovedBy.auto: since 1.21 (spec/plan-auto-approve.md), plan only: a flow v2 module's tasks/<id>/plan.md exists; a v2 Plan is approved by being written, whatever marker it carries (review still reports the raw marker), and it is never listed in awaitingReview
reviewApprovedBy.null: per module, per file: no approval in effect -- no marker, pending, revised, invalid, or Codex's approval where the takeover does not let it count (such a file is listed in awaitingReview); an important requirement's Spec approved by Codex is null too

codexRoute.null: the module's takeover gives this step to Codex and no user approval is required
codexRoute.takeover: the module's takeover does not give this step to Codex
codexRoute.important: the Spec is judged to be an important requirement
codexRoute.pre-declared: the Plan's pre-declared section has content or is malformed
codexRoute.requirement: since 1.19: a flow v2 module's requirement (spec/<id>.md), which only the user confirms whatever the takeover; review-mark refuses codex-approved on it (codex-route-requirement)
codexRoute.auto: since 1.21, plan only: a flow v2 module's Plan, approved automatically and reviewed by nobody, also before it is written; review-mark refuses --target plan and both on the module (plan-auto)

importantReasons.multi-module: per module, in important.reasons (interface 1.15, spec/important-requirement.md): inserted into the capability map in one batch with another module; old-flow modules only since 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md: a flow v2 module is important on risk-path only)
importantReasons.cross-module: the Spec's concurrency boundary lists shared file categories, or its exclusive paths overlap another unfinished module's; old-flow modules only since 1.27
importantReasons.cross-unknown: the Spec has no concurrency boundary to judge by; only listed where the module's takeover gives the Spec to codex (Q7 A)
importantReasons.risk-path: a boundary path or a pre-declared public path matches a T3 or T4 pattern in .github/autopr/risk-paths.json (autopilot.risk-paths/v1)
importantReasons.risk-unknown: that list is missing or unreadable; only listed where the module's takeover gives the Spec to codex

progressFacts.appearsWhen: always, whatever moduleConcurrency is (interface 1.2; gates since 1.3, gate criterion changed in 1.4, Chinese checkpoint forms counted since 1.6)

fields.uncommittedTicks: per module; checked items in this checkout's working-tree tasks/<id>/todo.md minus those at HEAD, never below 0; an untracked todo counts every checked item; null when history is unavailable. Other worktrees are not counted: read worktree.dirty and worktree.progress
fields.startedAt: per module; commit time (%cI) of the first commit in HEAD's history that added spec/<id>.md; null when the Spec was never committed or history is unavailable; in a shallow clone it may be the first commit after the shallow boundary; it is a commit time, not when writing began, so a project that commits the Spec only after approval gets a later time than the actual start
fields.head.committedAt: commit time (%cI) of HEAD of this checkout, for the whole checkout and not per module; null without commits
fields.reviewCadence: top level; {"value", "source"}, the same effective value and source /spec-guard:config shows; source is .agent/config.json, default, or default (config invalid)
fields.gates: per module (interface 1.3, spec/map-gate-count.md; criterion changed in 1.4, spec/checkpoint-default-report.md; checkpoint forms widened in 1.6, spec/cn-checkpoint-gates.md); {"total", "done"}: the gate checkpoints in this checkout's working-tree tasks/<id>/todo.md and how many of them are checked; a checkbox item is a checkpoint when it starts with Checkpoint or 检查点, or when the part before its first colon (the whole item when there is none) carries a tier such as 最终验收（gate） (since 1.6; before 1.6 only Checkpoint items counted, so total may be larger than under 1.5); the tier is read before the first colon: (gate) counts, (report) does not, and an untiered checkpoint counts only when it is the last checkpoint of the todo (since 1.4 untiered middle checkpoints are reports and no longer counted, so total may be smaller than under 1.3); the same criterion as nextGate; the final acceptance is normally the last gate and is already in total, so do not add it again when counting a baseline; null when the todo does not exist; does not need git history

reviewCadence.separate: default; the Spec is approved on its own before the Plan is written
reviewCadence.combined: the Spec and the Plan are approved together, unless the rules send the Spec back to be approved alone

progressFacts.notes: facts only: spec-guard sets no threshold and makes no stalled judgement; readers decide how long is too long

fields.deferred: per module; [{"item", "resumeWhen"}] of the formal deferrals in this checkout's working-tree tasks/<id>/todo.md, in order; an unchecked item written `- [ ] 延期：<item>；恢复条件：<condition>` or `- [ ] Deferred: <item>; Resume when: <condition>` (prefixes case-insensitive, either colon and semicolon form, languages may mix); an item that is a checkpoint or has an empty condition is not a deferral; [] when there is none or no todo
fields.deferredTotal: top level; the sum of every module's deferred items

deferral.statusChange: since 1.12 a formal deferral is not an unchecked item: a module whose only unchecked items are deferrals has status done (before 1.12 in_progress) and its dependents can be ready; progress.total and the stage hint's counts leave deferrals out; status values are unchanged; projects without deferrals see no change

fields.spec: the Spec's approval route: null, takeover, important, pre-declared or requirement (see values.codexRoute)
fields.plan: the Plan's approval route: null, takeover, important, pre-declared or auto (see values.codexRoute)

codexRoute.meaning: the same module_stage.codex_route(root, module, kind) decision used by reviewMark to refuse codex-approved when nonempty; an empty result is JSON null. Computed even when the Spec or Plan file is missing, independently of its approval marker

fields.spec: the Codex review rounds recorded in spec/<id>.md, in file order; [] when the file is missing or has no round line
fields.plan: the Codex review rounds recorded in tasks/<id>/plan.md, in file order; [] when the file is missing or has no round line

entryFields.round: the round number written by reviewMark (codex-approved or codex-reviewed)
entryFields.blocking: the number of blocking findings in that round's report
entryFields.sha256: the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of the reviewed Spec or Plan bytes in that round -- the file's value in the delegate report's scope.files, not a hash of the report file; the round line keeps only this prefix, not the full digest

reviewRounds.meaning: facts read from the round lines <!-- spec-guard: codex-review round=N blocking=N sha256=<12 hex> --> outside code fences, the same reading reviewMark uses for its two-round cap; every round is listed, also from before a revision, whatever the approval marker says now. No verdict is derived here: a caller checks a Codex approval or the two-round hand-off against reviewApprovedBy and codexRoute itself. An unreadable Spec or Plan fails the whole view (exit 4) like review

flow.appearsWhen: per module, always (interface 1.18, spec/flow-doc-skeletons.md; requirementConfirm since 1.19)

fields.tier: the flow v2 tier from the line <!-- spec-guard: flow v2 tier=<tier> --> in spec/<id>.md: bug, small, normal or important; an unknown tier reads as normal, and important when the rules judge the requirement important (see important); null for a module without the line (the old Spec -> Plan flow, unchanged)
fields.requirementConfirm: since 1.19 (spec/requirement-confirm-gate.md): null for an old-flow module; for a flow v2 module {status, by, at, sha256}: status is one of requirementConfirmStatus; by is "user" when confirmed, else null; at is the commit time (ISO 8601) of the earliest commit in the unbroken run back from HEAD whose spec/<id>.md carries the current approval line (outside code fences), null when not confirmed, not committed, outside git, or more than 50 commits of the file back; sha256 is the 12-hex prefix of the sha256 of the whole file, as spec-digest.py text prints it (the same kind of value as reviewRounds.sha256). An unreadable spec/<id>.md fails the whole view (exit 4) like review
fields.requirementReview: since 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md): null for an old-flow module; for a flow v2 module {required, status, records}: required is true when the effective tier is normal or important (a bug or small the rules lift included); status is not-required, missing (required and no record: the requirement cannot be confirmed, reviewMark refuses with requirement-unreviewed) or reviewed (one record is enough; later edits do not undo it); records lists, in file order, {reviewer: codex (a codex-review round line), host (<!-- spec-guard: requirement-review reviewer=host blocking=N sha256=<12 hex> -->) or none (<!-- spec-guard: requirement-review reviewer=none sha256=<12 hex> reason=<one line> -->), blocking, sha256 (the 12-hex prefix of the whole file's sha256 when reviewed), reason (none only, else null)}. The findings themselves are in the requirement's external review section
fields.overallDesign: since 1.26 (spec/sg-gate-flow.md): null for an old-flow module or when spec/<id>.md has no line <!-- spec-guard: overall-design spec/overall/<name>.md -->; else {path, status}: path is that file (null when the line or path is malformed), status is one of overallDesignStatus. Only the user approves it (review-mark --target overall); a Codex or reviewer marker reads as pending. A confirmed requirement whose overall design is not approved holds the module before its design

stepValues.design: since 1.18, flow v2 normal/important modules only: the requirement is written, tasks/<id>/design.md is not (stage hint NEEDS_DESIGN)
stepValues.regression: since 1.18, flow v2 normal/important modules only: the design is written, tasks/<id>/regression.md is not (stage hint NEEDS_REGRESSION)

flow.meaning: bug and small modules write one document (spec/<id>.md) and go from the requirement straight to the Plan; normal and important modules write the design and the regression document first. Document sections: references/doc-skeletons.md. step keeps spec, plan and build for every other case. A flow v2 requirement waiting for the user (requirementConfirm.status pending or revised, also with no approval line) is listed in awaitingReview with its raw review value

requirementConfirmStatus.confirmed: the user's approval line, its digest matching the text
requirementConfirmStatus.pending: no approval line, review pending, or only Codex's approval (digest matching or not): Codex never confirms a requirement
requirementConfirmStatus.revised: the user approved it, then the text changed; the user confirms it again
requirementConfirmStatus.invalid: the approval line is malformed (see review)

designApproval.appearsWhen: per module, always (interface 1.20, spec/design-review.md); null for an old-flow module and for flow v2 bug and small modules, which have no design

fields.approvedBy: user or reviewer when status is approved, else null
fields.reviewerVendor: the last round's reviewer vendor (delegate report reviewer.vendor, e.g. openai or anthropic); null when no round was recorded or the last one had no reviewer available
fields.sameVendor: the last round's reviewer.same_vendor (true when the reviewer is from the same vendor as the host that wrote the design; recorded, not judged); null like reviewerVendor
fields.reportSha256: the full sha256 of the last round's report file, from the round line's report field; null like reviewerVendor
fields.rounds: every design review round in tasks/<id>/design.md, in file order: the reviewRounds entry fields plus vendor and sameVendor (both null for a round with no reviewer available), and since interface 1.27 reportSha256 (that round's report sha256)
fields.reason: interface 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md): why the design is reviewed, the first of reasons; null when it needs no review. risk-path (an impact path, the module's own documents left out, is on the T3/T4 risk-path list), irreversible (the interface and data section has content other than one of 不涉及/无/没有/None/N/A/Not applicable/No changes), new-dependency (the impact lists a dependency manifest or lock file), configured (none of these and designReview is on). old-files and impact-unknown no longer appear from interface 1.27
fields.reasons: interface 1.27: every review reason that applies, in the order risk-path, irreversible, new-dependency; [configured] when only the switch applies; [] when none
fields.riskList: interface 1.27: ok when a risk-path list is readable, no-list when not (then risk-path is not checked, neither a hit nor a miss, and the phase hint says so)

statusValues.not-required: the design needs no review (no reason applies and designReview is off) and the takeover's design item is reviewer
statusValues.pending-review: a second reviewer must review it and no round is recorded yet (also before the design is written)
statusValues.in-review: the last round had blocking items (unresolved recheck items plus findings that are not suggestions); the second round rechecks the first
statusValues.pending-user: the user approves it: the takeover's design item is human (after the review when one is needed), or two rounds still blocking. Since interface 1.27 an important requirement follows the takeover like any other
statusValues.approved: passed: by the user (the approval line) or by the reviewer (reviewer-approved, when the takeover's design item is reviewer, an important requirement included since interface 1.27); the digest matches the design without its external review section
statusValues.unreviewed: the last round found no reviewer available (report reviewer.selection none); the user approves it
statusValues.revised: the design changed after it was approved or passed; it is reviewed or approved again

designApproval.meaning: facts from the approval line and the round lines <!-- spec-guard: design-review round=N blocking=N sha256=<12 hex> vendor=<v> same-vendor=<true|false> criteria=design-v1 report=<64 hex> --> outside code fences, written by reviewMark --target design. Whether a design needs review (interface 1.27): risk-path, irreversible or new-dependency (see reason) -> reviewed; designReview on -> reviewed; else not required. Who approves it is the takeover's design item alone. An unreadable design fails the whole view (exit 4) like review

acceptance.appearsWhen: per module, always (interface 1.15, spec/codex-final-acceptance.md); null for a flow v2 module (interface 1.24: verified against its regression document, see verification) and unless the module's takeover has merge=auto and the common git directory (or the legacy checkout location) holds its Codex acceptance record

fields.marker: always codex-approved: Codex accepted the final patch, with a non-author's check evidence on the same commit; the user's own final acceptance is the ticked final gate in the todo and has no record
fields.sha: the full commit the acceptance is about (HEAD when it was recorded); the phase hint treats the final gate as passed while it is HEAD or an ancestor of HEAD. Since interface 1.16 the record is `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/spec-guard/acceptance/<id>.json` (fields marker, sha, module, report_sha256, report as an absolute path, at): a record written in a linked worktree is also readable from the main checkout and other worktrees. Records written by interface 1.15 at the `--git-path` location are still read as a fallback; a valid record at the new location takes priority. Records are never migrated, deleted or committed

verification.appearsWhen: per module, always (interface 1.24, spec/verification-criteria.md); null for an old-flow module and for a flow v2 module with no recorded pre-merge verification

fields.verdict: pass, pass-with-notes or fail, from the recorded report
fields.patchId: the patch the verdict is about (git patch-id --stable of merge-base..head)
fields.notes: the titles of the report's notes, in order
fields.reportSha256: sha256 of the report file's bytes when it was recorded
fields.current: true while the recorded patchId equals the current patch (merge-base of the default branch and HEAD, to HEAD) and the regression document's sha256 is unchanged; only a current verdict other than fail counts as passed, and for a merge=auto module it passes the final gate

usageVerification.appearsWhen: top level, always (interface 1.24, Q2 A): {name: verification or null} for each spec/usage/<name>.regression.md, {} when there is none; the value has the same fields as verification

fields.milestoneStop: top level; null when the project has no usage draft (spec/usage/*.md) or no milestone is waiting; {"file": "spec/usage/<requirement>.md", "milestone": "M<n>", "modules": [...], "usages": ["U<n>", ...], "blocking": true|false} for the first milestone (drafts by file name, milestones in table order) whose modules all have status done and which has no confirmation line naming exactly those modules; {"error": "unreadable", "detail": ...} when a draft cannot be read or names a module not in the map (never null in that case)

milestoneStop.blocking: since 1.26 (spec/sg-gate-flow.md): false only when every module of the milestone names the autopilot preset (takeover.preset); the stage hint then only reports it and a caller does not hold new modules back. true otherwise, with the meaning below. The error object carries no blocking
milestoneStop.meaning: when blocking is true, the stage hint stops at this milestone until the user passes it and /spec-guard:milestone-mark records it; a caller that dispatches modules by this view should start no new module meanwhile, whichever milestone or draft it belongs to (modules not in any draft included), and lets modules already in progress finish; startable, stage and every other field are unchanged

takeover.appearsWhen: always, on every module, whatever moduleConcurrency is (interface 1.15, spec/takeover-config.md)

fields.design: per module; human or reviewer, in effect. Since 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md) the configured value alone: an important flow v2 requirement no longer forces human
fields.merge: per module; human or auto: whether a merge may be automatic
fields.release: per module; human, prepare, auto-confirm or auto: how far a release may go without the user
fields.spec: deprecated since 1.22, removed in the next version: human or codex, who approves an old-flow module's Spec (the old meaning of the value; reported for every module, meaningless for flow v2 modules, whose requirement is always the user's)
fields.plan: deprecated since 1.22, removed in the next version: human or codex, who approves an old-flow module's Plan (as spec; a flow v2 Plan is approved automatically, see codexRoute.plan)
fields.designForcedBy: since 1.22; always null since 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md: nothing forces design any more). Kept so readers checking the key still find it; was important when an important flow v2 requirement forced design to human
fields.source: per module; moduleTakeover (the module's own entry), takeover (the project value), default (nothing set) or default (config invalid) (the file, takeover or moduleTakeover is invalid; the items are then the next layer's)
fields.widerThanProject: per module; true when any item is wider than the project's effective item (the configured design, merge and release, orders as in takeover.items; the forcing by an important requirement is not counted); spec-guard only reports it and never caps
fields.narrowed: per module; null when the scope the module reads (its own moduleTakeover entry, else the project) has no narrowing record; else {"from", "source", "at"}: the value before the first narrowing, who narrowed last and when (takeover-narrow). The caller-written reason is never included
fields.releasePreauth: since 1.26 (spec/sg-gate-flow.md): per module; null for an old-flow module or when the effective release is not auto-confirm or auto; true when spec/<id>.md carries the line <!-- spec-guard: release-preauth yes --> and the user's confirmation of the requirement stands (the line is inside its digest, so an edit after the confirmation voids both); false otherwise (no line, another value, not confirmed, or confirmation voided). Whether it is void by a T4 change or a major version is autopilot's to judge; a caller that cannot read it treats it as null
fields.preset: since 1.26: per module; the preset name the effective value names -- a preset string (the old plan reads as none), or the "preset" key of a custom object; null for an object without one. Taken from the same layer as the items (moduleTakeover, takeover, default)

takeover.meaning: the same value project_config.module_takeover(root, id) returns; autopilot reads design, merge and release; module-crew reads spec and plan until 1.22's deprecation ends; spec-guard only stores and reports it, the callers act on it and enforce the release limits

concurrency.appearsWhen: only when .agent/config.json has moduleConcurrency set to on; otherwise none of these fields appear

fields.buildOrderGroups: top level; the Build order as a list of groups, a comma group being one inner list
fields.startable: top level; {"modules": every ready module in Build order, "conflicts": [{"modules": [a, b], "paths": [...]}] for unfinished modules whose exclusive paths overlap, a before b in Build order}; interface 1.8: with the switch on, a current module that is only the next one in Build order (no activeModule, no Spec, no Plan) counts as ready and is listed; an activeModule named in .agent/state.json stays in progress; top-level activeModule and stage are unchanged
fields.scope: per module; null without a concurrency boundary section, {"exclusive": [...], "shared": [...]} when valid, {"error": "<code>"} when malformed
fields.worktree: per module; null without a worktree carrying this module's role, else {"path", "branch", "head", "progress", "todo", "dirty", "merged"} plus "duplicates" when several worktrees claim it; merged is commit ancestry only (true, false, or null when unknown) and authorises nothing

values.off: default; spec-guard behaves exactly as without the switch
values.on: planning-layer rules for developing several modules at once apply: concurrency assessment, concurrency boundaries, the /map fields above, checkout roles

moduleConcurrency.readFrom: read mapView's top-level moduleConcurrency; absent means off. Readers need not open .agent/config.json

exitCodes.0: ok; stdout is {"module", "base", "files": [{"path", "status": "A|M|D|?", "scope"}], "outside": count, "declared": count}; base is the one used (interface 1.15: without --base, the parent of the commit that first added spec/<id>.md)
exitCodes.2: usage error, not a git repository, invalid module id, or the base is not a commit; or (1.15) no --base and the Spec has no earlier commit to compare with (base-unknown)
exitCodes.3: moduleConcurrency is not on and the module's takeover is none; nothing was checked (interface 1.15: a takeover module is checked with the switch off)
exitCodes.4: the module Spec has no concurrency boundary section, or it is malformed

scope.exclusive: inside one of the module's exclusive paths
scope.own: the module's own spec/<id>.md or tasks/<id>/
scope.outside: outside the boundary (shared categories included); reported, and for a takeover module the stage hint stops and hands it to the user (interface 1.15)
scope.declared: outside the boundary but a public path the approved, unchanged Plan pre-declares (interface 1.15, spec/takeover-scope-check.md)
scope.flow: a takeover module's change to spec/CAPABILITY-MAP.md or spec/usage/*.md (interface 1.15): add-module edits them next to the Spec and the user reviews them, so they are not overreach; since 0.91.1 also .agent/config.json, the project setting that narrowing or adjusting the takeover rewrites, and .agent/state.json, whose activeModule changes at module boundaries

checkoutRole.confirm: setModule, setCoordinator and clear only preview ("role: <old> -> <new>") unless --confirm is added
checkoutRole.marker: the file at `git rev-parse --git-path spec-guard/role` of that checkout: never committed and not shared between worktrees, so each worktree is set on its own

exitCodes.2: refused: not the top of a non-bare checkout, module not in the capability map, or the marker or its directory is a link or not a regular file
exitCodes.3: moduleConcurrency is not on (set and clear only)
exitCodes.4: the marker does not read back as written (a concurrent change); check it with show, do not retry blindly

role.module <id>: a module checkout: the stage hint also reports this module and points its next step only at it
role.coordinator: the coordinating checkout: the stage hint keeps review constraints and never suggests building

exitCodes.2: refused: module not in the capability map, file missing, invalid marker, or approving a Plan while its Spec is pending, revised or invalid; for codex-approved and codex-reviewed also: no --review, a report that is not a completed Codex review with a conclusion or does not match the file on disk, blocking findings (codex-approved), two rounds with blocking findings already, or --target both; for codex-approved also (since 1.16, spec/codex-route-guard.md): codex-route-takeover, codex-route-important, codex-route-pre-declared or (since 1.19) codex-route-requirement when the module's takeover does not let Codex approve this file (the same decision as mapView.codexRoute), checked before the report is read and with nothing written; for --target acceptance: a state other than codex-approved, no --review, a module whose takeover is not merge=auto (since 0.91.1 also in the commit before the module started: acceptance-not-auto-at-base), uncommitted changes, a final review that is not a clean Codex review up to HEAD with the Spec on disk, missing or failing check evidence for HEAD, or files outside the module's declared scope; for --target design (since 1.20, spec/design-review.md): a module that is not flow v2 normal or important (design-not-v2), a codex-* state (design-state), and for reviewer-approved and reviewer-reviewed also: no --review, a report that is not a delegate design-v1 review of the file on disk (report-invalid), two rounds with blocking items already (design-rounds-exhausted), a round after a blocking one without recheck (design-recheck-missing), criteria different from earlier rounds (design-criteria-changed), or blocking items (reviewer-approved: design-blocking); reviewer-* with another target (reviewer-state); since 1.21 (spec/plan-auto-approve.md): --target plan or both on a flow v2 module (plan-auto), before any file is read, whatever the state; since 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md): approved on --target spec for a flow v2 requirement of effective tier normal or important with no review record (requirement-unreviewed); codex-reviewed, host-reviewed or no-reviewer on --target spec when such a requirement already has a record (requirement-review-recorded: one round only); host-reviewed without --blocking (blocking-missing) or with nothing but record lines in the external review section (review-findings-missing); no-reviewer on --target spec without a valid one-line reason, at most 200 characters, without -- or > (requirement-review-reason); host-reviewed or no-reviewer on another target, or on --target spec for any other module (no-report-state)

reviewMark.notes: approved is written only after the user's explicit approval of that file; with moduleConcurrency on, the coordinating session writes it on the integration checkout (shared rule: the coordinating session's approvals and merges). codex-approved and codex-reviewed (interface 1.15, spec/codex-approval.md) take the /delegate:review JSON saved to a file; each records one round line under the external review section, and codex-approved also writes the Codex marker. Codex's approval is spec-guard's policy under the takeover setting, not the user's approval. --target acceptance --state codex-approved --review <final review> (interface 1.15, spec/codex-final-acceptance.md) records Codex's final acceptance of HEAD for a merge=auto module in the common git directory (since interface 1.16; see mapView.acceptance); the check evidence is read from ~/.autopilot/evidence/<owner>__<repo>/<HEAD>.json (autopilot.check-evidence/v1); nothing tracked is written and the final gate is ticked after the merge. --target design (interface 1.20, spec/design-review.md) works on tasks/<id>/design.md of a flow v2 normal or important module: pending and approved (the user's) as for a Spec; reviewer-reviewed and reviewer-approved take the /delegate:review --profile design JSON from any backend and record one design-review round line (see mapView.designApproval), blocking counting unresolved recheck items plus findings that are not suggestions; reviewer-approved also writes `<!-- spec-guard: review reviewer-approved <digest> -->`. A report with reviewer.selection none is recorded as unreviewed (vendor=none) and leaves the design pending for the user. Since 1.27 (spec/sg-review-rules.md): --target design accepts host-reviewed --blocking N (a fresh host subsession's review: a round line with vendor=host same-vendor=true criteria=host report=none; with 0 it also writes the reviewer-approved marker) and no-reviewer (vendor=none criteria=none report=none, unreviewed), and checks the effective tier, so a bug or small the rules lift to important can record its design; --target spec accepts host-reviewed --blocking N and no-reviewer --reason for a requirement's one review round (record lines in requirementReview), leaving the approval marker as it is. Confirming a reviewed requirement previews the changes since the review, both sides without the approval marker and the external review section

reviewKinds.appearsWhen: always (interface 1.5); add-only: kinds and section names are never renamed or removed within 1.x
reviewKinds.description: the kinds of user decision spec-guard's shared checkpoint rules produce, with the sections each one shows in the conversation, in order. Every kind needs a reply; the recommended reply sits in one copyable code block unless the installed collaboration plugin rules where the user answers. Kinds spec-guard does not produce (go-to-session, interface proposals) are not listed
reviewKinds.field: each key is the code of the session-protocol 【等待用户】「类型」 value (values defined in contract v2.3 and unchanged through v2.6); label is the value written there

plan.label: Plan
sections: 中途会停下来问你的地方

spec-plan.label: Spec 与 Plan
sections: 中途会停下来问你的地方
spec-plan.notes: reviewCadence combined: the Spec sections, then the Plan sections, approved at once

stuck.label: 卡住选做法
stuck.notes: not an approval but needs a reply: the same goal failed a second time for an outside reason; each option with its cost

reviewKinds.commonLinesNote: separate lines after the sections, not sections themselves; 注意 says 无 when empty

renamedSections.note: session-protocol v2.6 upstream names; spec-guard writes the new names, both stay valid, the old names in kinds stay until 2.0

exitCodes.0: ok: preview, ticked, or the final gate is already ticked (no change)
exitCodes.2: refused, nothing changed; the output starts with not-a-module-id, map-unreadable, not-in-map, todo-missing, todo-unreadable, no-gate, or not-at-final-gate (the first unchecked item is not the module's last gate; the item is printed)

gateTick.notes: interface 1.7; ticks only the final gate's checkbox in tasks/<id>/todo.md, by the same criterion as the stage hint's final gate (gates and nextGate use it too, Chinese checkpoint forms included); ordinary items after it are left and counted; the rest of the line and its line ending are kept; never commits; the caller must already hold the user's approval of the final acceptance, as with reviewMark

exitCodes.0: ok; stdout is {"conflicts": [{"modules": [a, b], "paths": [...], "sources": {a: <spec-file or "project">, b: ...}}], "errors": [{"module": <id or null>, "source": <spec-file or "project">, "error": <code>}]}; a Spec without a usable boundary is listed in errors and left out, the rest are still compared
exitCodes.2: usage error, nothing compared: neither --spec nor --project, a --spec not in <module-id>=<file> form, an invalid or repeated module id, or --project is not a directory

source.<spec-file>: the --spec file path as given; it replaces the project's spec/<id>.md for that module
source.project: spec/<id>.md of a module that /map reports in_progress or ready in --project

error.no-boundary: the Spec has no concurrency boundary section
error.missing-exclusive: the boundary section has no exclusive line
error.unknown-line: a line in the boundary section that is neither exclusive nor shared
error.unreadable: the Spec file cannot be read as UTF-8
error.no-capability-map: --project has no spec/CAPABILITY-MAP.md; only the --spec files were compared
error.map-unreadable: the capability map or a module file under --project cannot be read; only the --spec files were compared

scopeOverlap.notes: interface 1.10; --spec is repeatable and --project is optional, at least one is required; relative --spec paths resolve against the working directory; runs whatever moduleConcurrency says; every pair is compared, overlap is the same rule as mapView startable.conflicts (equal paths, or one inside the other's directory; the narrower path is listed); modules are ordered by Build order, modules not in the map follow in --spec order

exitCodes.0: ok; stdout is {"module", "planApproved", "approvedCommit", "declared", "publicPaths": [...], "dependencies": [{"name", "range"}], "configs": [...], "patches": [...]}; declared is false when tasks/<id>/plan.md is missing or has no pre-declared section, and the four lists are then empty
exitCodes.2: usage error, nothing read: invalid module id, the module is not in the capability map, the capability map cannot be read, or --project is not a directory
exitCodes.4: the Plan's pre-declared section is malformed or the Plan cannot be read; stdout is {"module", "error": <code>} with no approval facts

planApproved.true: the working-tree Plan's marker is approved and the file is byte-for-byte the version of approvedCommit
planApproved.false: anything else: not approved, edited after approval (committed or not), approval not committed, not a git repository, or the approving commit is not in the history

values.approvedCommit: the latest commit that made the Plan's marker approved, only when planApproved is true; otherwise null

error.bad-path: a path is malformed (wildcard, absolute, .., not in backticks), or a config or patch is written as a directory
error.bad-dependency: a dependency is not `name@range`, has an empty part or whitespace, or its range starts with workspace:
error.unknown-line: a line that is none of the four, or one of them twice
error.unreadable: the Plan cannot be read as UTF-8

declaredScope.notes: not limited by moduleConcurrency; deleting files, changing outward contracts and security exceptions cannot be pre-declared (rule text only, not detected here)

presets.none: default; design, merge and release all human
presets.autopilot: since 1.26 (spec/sg-gate-flow.md): design=reviewer, merge=auto, release=auto-confirm; never the factory default, a project or module names it. A custom object may carry "preset": <name> (any preset above) and override items: {"preset": "autopilot", "release": "human"}; without it unnamed items read as human

takeover.readFrom: python3 -B hooks/map_view.py --json --project <project-root>: each module's takeover; or project_config.module_takeover(root, id). The raw value is the item whose key is takeover in project_config.py show --format json
takeover.writeWith: python3 -B hooks/project_config.py set --key takeover --value <preset|JSON object> [--confirm]; unset --key takeover [--confirm]; preview unless --confirm
takeover.notes: a preset name or a custom object of items (missing items read as human); any unknown item or value makes the whole key invalid. The requirement and a flow v2 Plan are not configurable. design: whether a normal flow v2 design is let through by the second reviewer (reviewer) or approved by the user (human, also every design that needs no review); an important requirement's design is always the user's. Items run from strictest to widest in the order listed. Release auto-confirm and auto are stored as given; the limits (the four pipeline plugins at most prepare, auto only where a release rolls back quickly) are hinted at in the preview and enforced by autopilot. Writing it needs the user's own words. spec-guard 0.84.0-0.94.0 read the preset design as invalid and ignore only this key; 0.68.0-0.83.x ignore the key; 0.67.1 and earlier treat the whole file as invalid. The file may also hold takeoverNarrowed (scope -> {from, to, source, reason, at}), written only by narrow and kept by set; config cannot set or unset it

legacy.meaning: since 1.22 (spec/takeover-redefine.md): old values stay valid and are read converted, never written (set refuses them, takeover-legacy). For a flow v2 module the old preset plan reads as none and the custom items spec and plan do not apply; old merge reads as the new merge. An old-flow module (no flow v2 marker) reads who approves its Spec and Plan from the old meaning: plan or design -> plan=codex; merge -> spec=codex, plan=codex; a custom object as written, with plan=codex where design=reviewer and plan is not written

moduleTakeover.readFrom: as takeover: each module's takeover in map_view.py --json, or project_config.module_takeover(root, id)
moduleTakeover.writeWith: python3 -B hooks/project_config.py set --key moduleTakeover --module <module-id> --value <preset|JSON object> [--confirm]; unset --key moduleTakeover [--module <module-id>] [--confirm]; one entry at a time, preview unless --confirm
moduleTakeover.notes: an object of module id -> takeover value; any bad entry makes the whole key invalid and every module falls back to the project value with source default (config invalid). A module without an entry follows takeover. Wider than the project is reported, never capped. Ids not in the capability map are warned by verify-artifacts and ignored by /map. Writing it needs the user's own words

source.autopilot: autopilot found a reverted auto-merge, a red main or a rollback after release
source.module-crew: module-crew found one of its incidents

takeoverNarrow.order: a preset steps merge -> design -> none (the old plan steps to none); a custom value hands back its first non-human item in the order release, merge, design (release goes straight back to human) and is written in the new form; a value with only old items left is written as none; all human is written as none; already the strictest writes nothing and exits 0. A record from the old plan is removed when set writes none or design
takeoverNarrow.scope: --module narrows that module (starting from the project value when it has no entry of its own) and writes its moduleTakeover entry; without it the project takeover is narrowed and module entries are left alone

exitCodes.0: narrowed, previewed, or already the strictest
exitCodes.2: bad --source, --reason or --module, or the configuration file cannot be written

takeoverNarrow.notes: no user words needed: narrowing is the safe direction (S101 Q6). Writes .agent/config.json, which the caller or the user then commits. Records takeoverNarrowed: the first from stays until the scope is restored to it; while the record exists, config set widens that scope at most one step at a time (exit 2 otherwise). Preview unless --confirm

exitCodes.0: ok; problems are listed in the output, not fatal
exitCodes.2: usage error, --project is not a directory, not a module id or usage name, or the module is not in the capability map
exitCodes.3: stdout is {"schemaVersion":1,"error":...} with not-flow-v2 (an old-flow module), no-document (the regression document is not written yet) or not-at-ref (with --ref: that commit has no capability map row or no such document)
exitCodes.4: stdout is {"schemaVersion":1,"error":"unreadable"}: a document is not UTF-8, the ref does not exist, or the clone at the ref failed

method.command: run the command; command is set
method.script: run the script; command is set
method.ai-operate: an agent operates the product (browser, app) and keeps the evidence
method.manual: the user checks; the evidence is the user's words and where they said them

problem.case-field-missing: a case lacks one of steps, expected, method, evidence (where: '<case id> <field>')
problem.case-method-invalid: the method is not command, script, ai-operate or manual
problem.case-command-missing: a command or script case has no command
problem.case-command-unexpected: an ai-operate or manual case has a command
problem.case-id-duplicate: the same R<n> twice in one document (where: '<document>:<line>')
problem.criterion-uncovered: a success criterion of the requirement has no row in the coverage table (where: the S<n>); not checked for bug or usage
problem.criterion-unknown: the coverage table names an S<n> the requirement (or, for --usage, the usage draft) does not have
problem.case-unknown: the coverage table names a case that does not exist
problem.affected-existing-empty: the design's impact lists files that existed before the module started, and the affected-existing section has no case
problem.module-unknown: --usage only: a module under 'Modules involved' is not in the capability map

values.fields: top level: schemaVersion, module (null for --usage), usage (null for --module), tier (null for --usage), document, sha256 (of the document's raw bytes; with --ref the raw blob), ref (as given, or null), criteria (S<n> of the requirement or usage draft), cases, problems [{code, where}]; --usage adds modules. Each case: id, title, steps, expected, method, command (null when absent), evidence, criteria (S<n> the coverage table maps to it), affectedExisting, sha256
values.caseSha256: sha256 of the compact JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8) of steps, expected, method, command, evidence, each with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space and trimmed; missing fields are empty strings; the id and the title are not part of it
values.documents: normal and important: tasks/<id>/regression.md; bug and small: the 回归用例 / Regression cases section of spec/<id>.md; --usage <name>: spec/usage/<name>.regression.md

regressionView.notes: interface 1.23 (spec/regression-doc-check.md); read-only. Markdown is parsed only here. command runs as written; for an earlier commit append refArgs (the view is built from a shared local clone checked out at that commit, documents read as raw blobs). usageCommand reads a multi-module requirement's integration regression.

exitCodes.0: author recorded (or already recorded); check: the report stands; record: previewed or written
exitCodes.1: the report does not stand; problems lists every code
exitCodes.2: usage error, not in the capability map, not a flow v2 module, unreadable report file, or no session id in the environment (author)
exitCodes.3: cannot judge: no author record (author-unknown), git unreadable, or no regression document

problem.report-invalid: the report is not JSON, not schema spec-guard.verification/v1, names another module, or a field has the wrong shape (where: which)
problem.regression-changed: regression.sha256 is not the current regression document's sha256
problem.case-missing: a case of the current regression document has no result
problem.case-unknown: the report has a case the document does not
problem.method-mismatch: a case's method differs from the document
problem.manual-without-user: a manual case has no user-quote evidence with a source
problem.fail-category-missing: a fail has no failCategory among run-failure, user-bug, check-failure, wrong-doc
problem.baseline-evidence-missing: a baseline-fail has no baselineCommit or no evidence, or the commit is not base or an ancestor of it
problem.evidence-sha-mismatch: an evidence file that can be read does not match its sha256 (unreadable files are listed as unverified)
problem.verdict-inconsistent: the verdict does not follow the cases: any fail gives fail; else notes give pass-with-notes; else pass
problem.executor-is-author: executor.sessionId is among the module's recorded authors
problem.patch-mismatch: patchId is not the current patch
problem.patch-id-wrong: base and head are readable and patchId is not their patch id (unreadable commits are listed as unverified)
problem.author-unknown: the module (for --usage: one of its modules) has no author record; exit 3, the check cannot judge

values.checkOutput: --json: {schemaVersion, established, verdict, patchId, problems [{code, where}], unverified [text]}; on a refusal {schemaVersion, error}
values.record: the common git directory, spec-guard/verification/<module>.json (usage-<name>.json for --usage): {schema, module, usage, verdict, patchId, base, head, regressionSha256, reportSha256, executor, notes [title], at}; never committed
values.authors: the common git directory, spec-guard/authors/<module>.json: [{sessionId, host, at}]; the session id comes only from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (host claude-code) or CODEX_THREAD_ID (host codex)

verification.notes: interface 1.24 (spec/verification-criteria.md). The commands run as written; append usageArgs in place of --module <module-id> for a multi-module requirement's integration regression, and confirmArgs to record. check is read-only; author writes without --confirm because it records the session's own fact, not an approval.
